turn1.explanation: The unit fires on the token that comes directly before a period '.', most strongly when that period is internal rather than sentence-final: decimal points (0.07, 29.9), domain or file-name dots (www., github.com), code member-access dots (e.target, local_params.delete) and abbreviation dots (N.C., R. 47.5, U.S., i.e.). Tokens before ordinary sentence-ending periods activate more weakly, though still noticeably.
turn1.evidence: Every top example marks the pre-dot token: '-0.07', 'www.aace.co.uk', 'e.target.classList', 'N.C.', 'local_params.delete', 'data: [29.9, 71.5', '2.000m2' and 'connect1.apple.com'. Mid-range examples are mostly abbreviations or sentence ends ('A. actinomycetemcomitans', 'Michelle K.', 'etc.', '3D gaming.', 'currently have.'), while 'P < 0.001' and 'i.e.' still reach 9-10.
turn1.missing_data: Tokens before other punctuation such as commas or colons, to confirm the unit is specific to periods. Whether the activation sits on the token before the dot or on the dot itself in tokenizers that split them differently.
